title: Pluggable runtime adapter for speculative decoding with quasi-randomized routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a pluggable runtime adapter that enables quasi-randomized model routing for speculative decoding, surfaces early acceptance metrics to the scheduler, and orchestrates deterministic fallback when acceptance confidence falls below thresholds. This ticket covers design, implementation of the adapter interface, lightweight acceptance signals, and integration tests with the decode scheduler and kernel selector.
background: Current speculative decode experiments are hardwired into the orchestration layer and rely on handcrafted heuristics (e.g., top-N preference / static priorities). This makes it difficult to iterate on routing policies and to A/B test acceptance thresholds or kernel-specific behavior. We need a modular adapter that can be swapped without changing the core scheduler, plus standardized early-acceptance metrics for downstream telemetry and SLOs.
proposed_solution: Build a small pluggable RuntimeAdapter interface with three responsibilities: 1) propose candidate model variants for speculative prefill + decode (supporting weighted/quasi-random selection), 2) compute an early-acceptance score (0.0-1.0) based on prefill probe outputs and kernel telemetry (latency, cache hits, token-entropy delta), and 3) recommend a fallback action when acceptance < threshold (switch to conservative model variant, increase batch priority, or offload to CPU-safe path). Implement one default adapter: "QuasiRandomRouter" that samples candidates using a weighted reservoir sampling seeded by request hash + entropy from recent telemetry, plus a lightweight AcceptanceEstimator that combines features into a logistic score. Expose config via per-customer routing policy in the control plane (can be toggled per route). Provide unit/integration tests and a small simulation harness for acceptance curve tuning.
acceptance_criteria: QuasiRandomRouter integrated with scheduler and used for 10% canary traffic
AcceptanceEstimator emits early_accept_confidence metric (tags: model_variant,kernel,fallback_action) per request
Fallback trigger executes and the request completes on fallback path within 2x latency of baseline for at least 99% of triggered fallbacks
Simulation harness can reproduce acceptance vs. quality tradeoff curve and export CSV for dashboarding
tasks: Define RuntimeAdapter proto and public method signatures (propose_candidates, score_acceptance, recommend_fallback)
Implement QuasiRandomRouter with configurable seed and per-candidate weight profile
Build AcceptanceEstimator feature extractor (prefill_confidence, kernel_latency_ratio, kv_cache_hit_rate, token_entropy_delta)
Wire adapter into decode scheduler with a 10% canary toggle and feature flag
Add telemetry: metrics, distributed traces, and request-level debug dump (sampled)
Create unit tests and integration tests including forced-fallback scenarios
Create simulation harness and scripts for parameter sweep (export CSV)
Prepare rollout plan, runbook, and dashboard panels in Console (prefill/acceptance metrics)
Docs: short dev guide + CHANGELOG entry
design_decisions: Pluggable adapter pattern to separate policy from scheduler core; adapter returns recommendations not commands
Quasi-randomized selection to avoid head-of-queue hotspots and enable low-variance exploration of model variants
AcceptanceEstimator uses a logistic regression-like score combining a few lightweight features to keep compute cost minimal during prefill
Fallbacks are orchestrated by scheduler but must be idempotent and bounded in latency impact
Telemetry tags chosen to allow per-kernel and per-variant aggregation without high cardinality: (model_variant, kernel_family, acceptance_bucket)
risks_mitigation: Risk: Quasi-random sampling might route too many requests to expensive variants — mitigate via configurable max-weight cap and per-customer spend guardrails
Risk: AcceptanceEstimator false positives could cause unnecessary fallbacks — mitigate via canary, offline simulation tuning, and conservative default thresholds
Risk: New metrics add cardinality — mitigate by limiting label cardinality and sampling debug traces
Risk: Regression in P99 latency during fallback storms — mitigation: circuit breaker in scheduler and immediate rollback path
timeline: Week 1: spec + proto + small prototype. Week 2: adapter + estimator implementation + unit tests. Week 3: integration with scheduler, telemetry, and canary rollout. Week 4: simulation runs, threshold tuning, dashboards, docs, and runbook. Contingency: extra week for bug fixes and wider rollout.
notes: Simulation harness will live in tools/speculative-sim. AcceptanceEstimator weights will be initially set from offline logistic fit over last 2 weeks of prefills. We must coordinate with Console to add early_accept_confidence to per-route dashboards before canary expands.
